Subject: Re: Control Plane split-brain tabletop & residency failover plan — preread (splitbrain-runbook-draft.pdf)

Folks — prepping a short preread for tomorrow's table-top. Key points I'd like to highlight so we align expectations:

1) Leader-election model: We use an epoch-based lease with a consensus-backed coordinator for control-plane leadership. Under a total partition, both regions may temporarily attempt leadership — the runbook enforces a lease-grace window and a quorum-based fencing approach before accepting a new leader.

2) Customer data paths: Note that data-plane (inference traffic) stays pinned to region unless explicit cross-region routing is enabled by the customer. That reduces GDPR/sovereignty exposure during failovers.

3) Automated rollback guard: If a control-plane change is applied during a partition, our recommended rollback is a staged rollback with coordinators in the majority region taking precedence; manual override only by authorized ops (2-of-3 approvers).

4) Observability: We recommend a preconfigured set of probes (leader-latency, lease-violations, controlplane-heartbeat) that trigger a playbook. We're including an initial alert-to-action mapping in the draft.

Attachments: splitbrain-runbook-draft.pdf, tabletop-exercise-notes-20270531.docx

I'll walk through the subsections quickly in the tabletop. Anything else to add to the preread?

—Vivek

Subject: Notes & actions from tabletop — control-plane split-brain (EU/APAC)

Thanks for a productive session today. Summary and explicit next steps: 

Summary:
- We exercised a scenario where the EU control plane lost peering to APAC during a rolling network maintenance. Two issues emerged: short-lived dual-leader attempts during transient flaps, and ambiguity around which region's control plane should drive dataset migrations if a failover is initiated.

Decisions & actions (owners):
- INF-8472: Add fencing enforcement to runbook (Vivek / due 2027-06-09)
- INF-8473: Add a residency-preserving migration flow to avoid cross-border temporary data movement (Hannah / due 2027-06-16)
- INF-8474: Update probes and alert playbooks, include threshold tuning for lease-grace window (Monica / due 2027-06-09)
- INF-8475: Document customer-facing guidance for on-prem peering changes (Markus / due 2027-06-14)

Attachments published: splitbrain-runbook-draft.pdf (v1), tabletop-exercise-notes-20270531.docx
Confluence: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SEC/Residency+and+Failover+Playbooks#SplitBrain
Jira: https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8472

If FinServ wants us to open a secured channel for sharing logs from their preprod clusters, we can do that — Oliver, please confirm. We'll follow up with the updated runbook once INF-8472/INF-8473 items land.

Best,
Lauren

Redwood Inference
